newsitem.title: HONG KONG: INSIGHT-Stage set for SHK Prop rebound.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Stage set for SHK Prop rebound.

text.p: Feb 11 * Suprt * Rstnce * MA-50 * MA-200
Properties 87.50 80.00 --
Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd appears to have completed a consolidation phase and could be set for a healthy rebound that will bring the share back onto its long-term uptrend, analysts said on Tuesday.

"The share has fallen to its 40-week (weighted) moving average and given past patterns could be set for a rebound from this level," said Chris Roberts, regional technical strategist at HSBC James Capel.
Using Fibonacci ratios on the weekly chart, the share has retraced 38 percent of its gain from the July low at HK$72.00, Roberts said.
"This decline looks like a correction," he said, adding that the share could resume its uptrend in the near term.
On Tuesday, Sun Hung Kai Properties fell HK$2.75, or three percent, to HK$88.25 on moderately heavy turnover of HK$389.31 million.
The share led the market down in late afternoon, when the Hang Seng Index fell to a low of 13,380.02 before recovering to close 189.33 points lower at 13,454.21.
Relative strength on the weekly chart is testing the 50-point level and Sun Hung Kai Properties shares could rebound if they do not break through that level, said Charles Cheung at J&A Securities.
"The share has built a platform at the HK$85.00 to HK$87.00 level," said Cheung.
A broker with a large UK house said property shares and the market as a whole needed a period of consolidation following the market's strong advance of the past year.
Sun Hung Kai Properties was often the market leader in 1996, until HSBC Holdings began its strong rally in the third quarter, brokers said.
The share rose 60 percent from HK$63.25 at the start of 1996 to an all-time high of HK$101.50 on November 28 before entering the current consolidation phase.
The share fell below HK$89.00 at the end of January following a recommendation by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority that banks cap luxury home mortgages at 60 percent of the property's value.
Brokers cited the same reason for the share's weakness on Tuesday.
"It is due to the (proposed) limitation on bank mortgages for luxury properties," said Francis Wu, institutional sales manager at South China Securities.
On the daily chart, the relative strenth indicator is still weakening at the 39-point level, suggesting some further weakness was possible before a rebound.
